ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: on the right side of the figure is a vertical wall, and on the wall a light rod is fixed with hinge O, with points A and C on the light rod; the two ends of a light rope are tied to A and C respectively, and the two sections of rope go downward around movable pulley B, with an object suspended below the movable pulley. In the first figure, the light rod AC is in a horizontal position; the second figure shows that after the light rod rotates around O, A and C are still on the same light rod, but the rod is inclined relative to the horizontal. Then reason: let the tension of the entire light rope be T. Since it is the same ideal light rope and goes around a smooth movable pulley, the magnitudes of the pulling forces of the rope on points A and C are the same, that is, F1=F2=T. Analyze the forces on the movable pulley and the object as a whole: the weight of the object is mg, and the magnitudes of the tensions in the two sections of rope are both T. Since when the system is at rest the resultant force in the horizontal direction is zero, the horizontal components of the two sections of rope must cancel each other out, so the angles between the two sections of rope and the vertical direction are equal, denoted as θ. Equilibrium in the vertical direction gives 2T cosθ=mg, so T=mg/(2cosθ). Then look at the geometric relationship: let the distance between A and C be d, the rope length AB+BC=L, and the angle between the light rod and the horizontal be α. The two sections of rope have the same angle θ with the vertical direction, so the horizontal projection between A and C is equal to L sinθ; while the horizontal projection of A and C on the light rod is d|cosα|, therefore L sinθ=d|cosα|. At the beginning α=0, and |cosα| is maximum, therefore sinθ is maximum and θ is maximum. After the light rod rotates from the horizontal position, |cosα| becomes smaller, so sinθ becomes smaller, θ becomes smaller, and cosθ becomes larger. From T=mg/(2cosθ), it can be known that T decreases. Since F1=F2=T, F1 and F2 both decrease.

method.method_draft: 先从图中读出：A、C 是同一轻杆上的两点，杆绕右端附近墙上的铰链 O 转动；一根轻绳两端系在 A、C，中间绕过动滑轮 B，B 下挂重物。图上初态杆 AC 水平，转动后 A、C 仍在同一直杆上但杆相对水平倾斜。由题文读出轻绳长度一定、动滑轮悬挂定质量物块，F1、F2 是绳对 A、C 的拉力大小。解题时设整根绳张力为 T，则理想轻绳和光滑动滑轮使 F1=F2=T。对动滑轮受力平衡：两段绳的水平分力必须相互抵消，因此两段绳与竖直方向夹角相等，设为 θ；竖直方向有 2T cosθ = mg。再用几何约束：设 AC=d，绳长 AB+BC=L，杆与水平夹角为 α。由于两绳段与竖直夹角同为 θ，A、C 间的水平投影等于 L sinθ，而杆上 A、C 间的水平投影为 d cosα，所以 L sinθ = d|cosα|。初态 α=0 时 sinθ 最大；杆从水平位置任意转动后 |cosα| 变小，故 sinθ 变小、θ 变小、cosθ 变大。由 T=mg/(2cosθ) 可知 T 减小，因此 F1、F2 均减小。

再推理：设整根轻绳的张力为 T。由于是同一根理想轻绳并绕过光滑动滑轮，所以绳对 A、C 两点的拉力大小相同，即 F1=F2=T。对动滑轮和物块整体受力分析，物块重力为 mg，两段绳的拉力大小均为 T。由于系统静止时水平方向合力为零，两段绳的水平分力必须相互抵消，因此两段绳与竖直方向的夹角相等，设为 θ。竖直方向平衡得 2T cosθ=mg，所以 T=mg/(2cosθ)。

再看几何关系：设 A、C 间距离为 d，绳长 AB+BC=L，轻杆与水平夹角为 α。两段绳与竖直方向夹角相同为 θ，所以 A、C 间的水平投影等于 L sinθ；而 A、C 在轻杆上的水平投影为 d|cosα|，故 L sinθ=d|cosα|。开始时 α=0，|cosα| 最大，因此 sinθ 最大、θ 最大。轻杆从水平位置转动后，|cosα| 变小，所以 sinθ 变小，θ 变小，cosθ 变大。由 T=mg/(2cosθ) 可知 T 减小。因为 F1=F2=T，所以 F1、F2 均减小。
